The exact launch timing for the iPhone Ultra remains unclear, as a new supply chain report indicates that Foxconn is making "final adjustments" to the production process. Earlier reports had suggested that mass production had already begun.

Recent reports suggest Apple will unveil a new foldable iPhone at its September event, though initial supply may be quite limited...

What is certain is that Apple has set stringent quality control standards for the production of its first foldable iPhone. The company held off on advancing the project until its display partner Samsung was able to produce a creaseless internal display.

These extremely high standards have made the product one of the most challenging Apple has ever released, and also mean production could be subject to delays. Beyond that, however, things are less clear.

Some earlier reports had suggested the iPhone Ultra launch could be significantly delayed, potentially not arriving until early next year. Subsequent reports pointed to a possible delay of just one to two months. The prevailing view now, however, is that even if this upcoming premium model is delayed, the postponement will not be lengthy.

Today's DigiTimes report doesn't actually provide much new information. The headline reads "Apple's first foldable iPhone faces production hurdles," but the content merely references what previous reports have already said and does not identify any new issues. The only specific claim is:

This situation may also simply be a normal part of the production process, rather than a malfunction requiring adjustment that could lead to production delays.

The tentative expectation therefore remains that it will debut alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and go on sale shortly afterwards, though initial supply may be relatively limited.
